title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in GitLab Integration
description: The GitLab integration allows users to configure a custom `instanceUrl` for self-hosted instances. While the URL is validated against a denylist using `validateInstanceUrl`, it fails to prevent SSRF because `validateInstanceUrl` allows resolving external domains that point to internal IP addresses (DNS rebinding / localtest.me). Additionally, the GitLab provider directly uses `fetch` instead of `safeFetch`, completely bypassing SSRF protections for DNS resolution time. This allows an attacker to make arbitrary authenticated HTTP requests to internal network services (e.g., metadata endpoints, internal APIs) via the `instanceUrl`.
root_cause: GitLabProvider in packages/integrations/src/providers/gitlab/provider.ts does not wrap HTTP requests in safeFetch to prevent SSRF via DNS rebinding, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery.
intended_behavior: Integration providers that connect to user-supplied URLs should use a safe fetch wrapper that resolves the hostname and checks the actual IP address against a denylist of private/internal networks before making the request, preventing DNS-based SSRF bypasses.

trace.description: Reads user-provided instanceUrl from the integration config.
Validates the URL using validateInstanceUrl, which is susceptible to DNS bypasses.
Calls fetch() directly with the attacker-controlled instanceUrl without additional IP-level validation.

conditions.description: User must have permission to configure an integration.

execution.attacker_perspective: A user with integration setup permissions configures a GitLab integration with a malicious custom instance URL.
instructions: Set the custom instance URL to a domain resolving to an internal IP (e.g., https://localtest.me).
Trigger an integration action (e.g., syncing projects) which causes the server to fetch from the internal IP.
execution.expected_result: The server sends an HTTP request to the internal IP address and returns the response or indicates connection success.

remediation.strategy: Implement and enforce a safe fetch wrapper (`safeFetch`) in `GitLabProvider` (and all other providers) that performs DNS resolution and checks the resolved IP against a denylist of private ranges before establishing the HTTP connection. Replace all direct `fetch` calls with `safeFetch`.

likelihood.reason: SSRF bypasses using DNS are well-known and trivial to exploit with services like localtest.me.

impact.reason: Allows access to internal network services, metadata endpoints, or other restricted APIs.

confidence.reason: The code clearly shows direct use of `fetch` with user-supplied domains, bypassing robust IP validation.
